orgDesign.companyProfile: Zaventem-based phygital brokerage and comparison group modeled on Peasy (peasy.be), the 2025 rebrand of Horizon Group that Vortex Capital Partners formed in 2020 around hypotheek.winkel, the mortgage brokerage chain started in 2001 that today runs about 70 largely franchised offices across Flanders and Brussels and compares the conditions of 25 banks daily, free of charge for the buyer because the chosen bank pays a referral commission. The group added Verzekeringen.be / Assurances.be in 2021 (insurance comparison across 11 insurers) and Aanbieders.be / Mesfournisseurs.be in 2022 (energy, telecom and mobile comparison and switching). Peasy reports more than 150 experts, 70 offices, more than 50,000 contracts concluded per year and more than 50 partners, employs roughly 200 people and generates revenues of around EUR 30 million; customer care operates from Hasselt and Oujda (Morocco), and an in-house academy trains about 30 advisors per year because mortgage experts are a scarce-skill role. In December 2025 Meilleurtaux (France; backed by Silver Lake; in Belgium since the 2023 acquisition of MiD Finance, mainly in Wallonia) agreed to acquire 100 percent of Peasy, creating a national platform with 81 offices led by Peasy CEO David Geerts for Belgium and Luxembourg. The organisation is modeled at about 200 people: head office, product and technology, customer care and the employed side of the office network; the experts on franchisee payroll are represented through the network team and its customers.
orgDesign.operatingModel: With about 200 people the group is an intermediation business with a small product and technology function inside it, not a software vendor: three groups and twelve teams. Product and Technology in Zaventem is six teams of four to eight people: five stream-aligned teams own the consumer comparison platform (simulators, feasibility certificate, upload-your-proposal, budget barometer, content and the multi-brand shell), the insurance, energy and telecom comparison modules with their partner catalogue, customer engagement (appointments, callbacks, the household contract vault, renewal monitoring and cross-sell), the mortgage expert workbench (daily bank rates, 25-bank comparison, advice record, credit file, bank submission and closing) and the brokerage tooling used by customer care (quote and bind, switch execution, cancellation, ticketing, lead routing); one platform team provides identity and consent, the integration gateway to banks, insurers, energy and telecom partners, e-signature and telephony, and the analytics platform. Advisory Network and Customer Care is the largest group by far: the hypotheek.winkel office network with about 150 experts in about 70 franchised offices, the customer-care centres in Hasselt and Oujda with about 45 advisors, the network development and franchise team that recruits offices and reports production and conversion, and the Peasy academy that certifies about 30 advisors a year. Partners, Finance and Compliance manages the contracts, tariff feeds and referral commissions of more than 50 banks, insurers, energy suppliers and telecom operators, pays out the office network, and keeps FSMA registrations, advice records, complaints and GDPR audit-ready across three brands. Because experts, franchisees and customer-care advisors are themselves customers of the platform (hexp, frnc, insa), friction in a file, a tariff feed or a switch reaches the product teams within days; the Meilleurtaux integration is run as a programme across the groups rather than as a separate team.

teams.name: Partner Management and Commissions
teams.description: Manage the relationships and the money with the more than 50 partners who pay the referral fees that keep the service free for consumers: the 25 banks whose conditions are compared daily, the 11 insurers, and the energy suppliers and telecom operators listed on Aanbieders.be.
